sections.title: Iran War and the Strait of Hormuz
sections.summary: Rubio sees deal as 'extremely difficult'; Tehran wants sanctions lifted first; tanker hit off Oman

paragraphs.heading: Talks stalled
paragraphs.body: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said a peace deal with Tehran is extremely difficult while attacks in the Strait of Hormuz continue, Al Jazeera reported. Iran's Supreme National Security Council said the strait will not reopen until the US 'corrects its behavior'. [[TAG:warning:no deal in sight]]

paragraphs.heading: Pakistan's mediation
paragraphs.body: Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir met President Masoud Pezeshkian in Tehran, Dawn reported. Pezeshkian said the US must 'end the pressure and threats and lift sanctions' before any negotiations. The New Arab reported Munir carried a new proposal backed by Pakistan and Qatar, which reportedly would release about $6 billion in frozen Iranian funds held in Qatar; Anadolu's sources said they did not know of any new proposal and that the visit focused on the Saudi-Houthi conflict. Security official Mohsen Rezaei said no enriched uranium would leave Iran, TRT World reported.

paragraphs.heading: Warning to the UN
paragraphs.body: Iran's UN envoy wrote to Secretary-General Antonio Guterres about the possible US use of the Massive Ordnance Air Blast bomb if fighting resumes after the midterms, Al Jazeera reported.

paragraphs.heading: Shipping attacks
paragraphs.body: A tanker was hit by an unknown projectile about 11 nautical miles off Bukha, Oman, on Wednesday and caught fire; all crew are safe, UKMTO said, according to Asharq Al-Awsat and Arab News. UKMTO's weekly assessment counted 12 attacks, 10 near Hormuz, with transits about 70% below prewar levels. The IRGC claimed three tankers hit mines on Tuesday, which Saudi Gazette reported but which has not been independently confirmed. [[TAG:danger:23 attacks in Oct]]

sections.title: Ukraine Diplomacy
sections.summary: Oslo talks called 'constructive'; Witkoff meets Putin as Russia frees Stephen Hubbard

paragraphs.heading: Oslo meeting
paragraphs.body: A US official told Reuters that Tuesday's Oslo talks between Zelensky, envoy Steve Witkoff and Norwegian, Finnish, European and NATO representatives were 'constructive' and made 'meaningful progress' toward a coordinated approach to Russia, The Week reported. Agenda items included 'Article 5-like' security guarantees, energy ceasefire proposals and postwar recovery. Foreign Policy described ties as strained, with Trump saying Zelensky 'is not helping matters much'.

paragraphs.heading: Witkoff in St. Petersburg
paragraphs.body: Russia released Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old Michigan native convicted of fighting as a mercenary for Ukraine, as Witkoff met Putin on Wednesday, ABC News, CBS News and CNN reported. Hubbard was the last American in Russia the State Department had designated as wrongfully detained; his family called the charges false. Witkoff brought new settlement proposals, UNN reported. As many as 10 other Americans remain in Russian custody. [[TAG:success:Hubbard released]]

paragraphs.heading: Starlink and intelligence
paragraphs.body: Rubio denied the White House ordered a Starlink slowdown for Ukraine and rejected as 'scandalous' claims that intelligence sharing was cut, NBC News and Yahoo News reported. Kyiv says the service still cuts out at speeds above about 161 km/h, too slow for interceptor drones to catch Russia's jet-powered Shaheds, Euromaidan Press reported. Ukraine has no access to the military-grade Starshield system, Rubio said. [[TAG:warning:disputed]]

sections.title: Markets and Earnings
sections.summary: Dow +530 on Tuesday; Netflix slides after hours; Kospi rebounds; Meta and Tesla report tonight

paragraphs.heading: Tuesday's close
paragraphs.body: The Dow rose 529.85 points, or 1.02%, to 52,495.88, led by 3M, while the S&P 500 gained 0.28% to 7,712.57 and the Nasdaq slipped 0.02% to 26,424.82, according to Capp Notes and Yahoo Finance. The VIX fell about 6% to 17.31. [[TAG:success:Dow +1%]]

paragraphs.heading: Netflix and GM
paragraphs.body: Netflix earned $0.87 a share, above the $0.82 consensus, on revenue of about $12.87 billion, but cut its 2026 advertising forecast to $2.7 billion from $3 billion, guided fourth-quarter earnings below estimates and announced 1,000 job cuts, Deadline and The Hollywood Reporter reported. Shares fell about 6% after hours. GM beat with adjusted earnings of $3.70 a share and approved a $20 billion buyback, but shares fell as much as 7% on cost and pricing worries, CNBC reported. [[TAG:danger:Netflix -6% AH]]

paragraphs.heading: Asia and oil
paragraphs.body: South Korea's Kospi rebounded about 3% on Wednesday after Tuesday's 3.7% drop, and Japan's Nikkei rose 0.9% as September exports jumped 16.7%, the AP reported via WSLS. Brent rose about 1.5% to near $110.38 in Asian trading after touching $111.99 on Tuesday, its highest since May, Oilprice.com and FinanceFeeds reported; API data showed US crude stocks fell 4.9 million barrels. [[TAG:warning:Brent ~$110]]

paragraphs.heading: Tonight
paragraphs.body: Meta and Tesla report after the close. Analysts expect Meta earnings of roughly $6.76–$6.80 a share and Tesla about $0.45, with options implying moves of about 7% for each, CNBC and Admiral Markets reported.

sections.title: US Politics
sections.summary: Trump rallies in North Carolina for trailing Whatley; Cook shifts two races toward Democrats

paragraphs.heading: North Carolina rally
paragraphs.body: Trump rallied in Greenville, North Carolina, for Senate nominee Michael Whatley, who trails Democrat Roy Cooper in recent polls, NBC News reported. Fox News said Trump invoked the 1988 Willie Horton case to attack Cooper's criminal justice record and announced a $1.5 billion federal investment in semiconductor production in the state. [[TAG:info:Senate battleground]]

paragraphs.heading: Map shifts
paragraphs.body: The Cook Political Report shifted two races toward Democrats and one toward Republicans, CNN reported. Trump said he plans to spend more than $400 million to help Republicans, and midterm ad spending is projected to exceed $11 billion. In New Hampshire, Republican John Sununu distanced himself from Trump in a new ad despite the president's endorsement.

sections.title: Europe
sections.summary: Italy sends 500 troops to Milan; Kallas says US pushing Kyiv to 'surrender on Putin's terms'

paragraphs.heading: Italy cracks down
paragraphs.body: Italy's cabinet approved deploying 500 troops to Milan and new laws on violent protest, including up to five years in prison for joining a threatening group of five or more, after weekend cost-of-living riots, Al Jazeera reported. Sources disagree on whether soldiers get police powers: Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said they would, but Italian media reported the cabinet dropped that after objections from President Sergio Mattarella. [[TAG:warning:troops deployed]]

paragraphs.heading: Wider unrest
paragraphs.body: The Rio Times' European roundup reported a curfew in parts of France, flooding in Marseille, Lisbon police arresting 55 housing protesters, and petrol bombs thrown at police in Tirana. Macron is touring the Gulf seeking energy deals to ease French fuel prices, Euronews reported.

paragraphs.heading: Kallas on Washington
paragraphs.body: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas told the European Parliament that US negotiators have spent about 18 months pushing Ukraine to 'surrender on Putin's terms' and that Europe needs a seat at the table, Euronews reported. Euronews said Trump's embrace of Putin has roiled Europe but not enough to break with the US. [[TAG:danger:transatlantic rift]]

sections.title: Israel and Lebanon
sections.summary: Tampa military talks end day one with low expectations; Lebanon rejects direct coordination

paragraphs.heading: Tampa talks
paragraphs.body: US-mediated military-technical talks between Lebanon and Israel at Central Command in Tampa ended their first day Tuesday and resume Wednesday, according to diplomatic sources cited by News Beep. Discussions focused on the June framework and 'pilot areas' in southern Lebanon from which Israeli forces are due to withdraw. Lebanon proposed halting Israeli demolitions, firing and military operations. [[TAG:info:day two today]]

paragraphs.heading: Low expectations
paragraphs.body: Lebanon plans to reject US-backed proposals for its army to coordinate directly with Israel's military, The National reported, and Lebanese officials told local media they saw no signs of optimism. Israel has sought to portray Lebanon's army as failing to disarm Hezbollah, The New Arab reported.
